newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares slip on drought concerns.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares slip on drought concerns.

text.p: Chilean stocks drifted lower on concerns about the effects of drought on profits in the power sector, brokers said.
After rising early in the day, the blue-chip IPSA index backtracked and ended 1.02 percent lower at 116.72 points, with big-volume electrical shares leading the declines.
The all-share .IGPA dipped 0.22 percent to 5352.40 points on light volume of 11 billion pesos traded.
Brokers were split on the effects of a series of Central Bank measures to lift restrictions on foreign exchange purchases for Chilean companies investing overseas.

Some said the effects were practically nil, while others said they hurt prices because brokers had expected the Bank to lift its reserve requirement on profits from American Depositary Receipts placed by Chilean companies. But it lifted the reserve requirment only on profits from direct foreign investment.
Electrical shares posted some of the steepest declines as concerns grew that power rationing would cut into profits.

Chilgener fell 2.5 percent to 167 pesos after its general manager, Juan Antonio Guzman, said on local television that rationing might be needed now, rather than in two or three weeks as planned by the government.

Enersis fell 3.2 percent to 241 pesos and Endesa was off 2.4 percent to 247 pesos. Severe drought in central and southern Chile dried up reservoirs used to power dam turbines. Chile depends on hydroelectric power for about 70 percent of its energy needs.

Rises included mining supply company Detroit Diesel, up 4.2 percent to 200 pesos on reports of a big increase in its first quarter net and paper pulp and oil conglomerate Copec, up 3.2 percent at 1625 pesos.
A welter of banking sector results failed to move the market either way as the numbers were generally in line with expectations, said brokers. Banco Santiago slipped 0.5 percent to 9.90 pesos.
